messages:
aj: Quick thread — during the 500->1k concurrent soak on canary today I repro'd a reproducible p99 tail when KV eviction rate climbs. p95 stayed ~120-140ms but p99 jumped 4x.
kai: Can you share the numbers and the config used? mb size, kernel hint, cache size?
aj: Run details: 1k clients, microbatch target 16, kernel hint 'auto', kv_capacity=50M entries, eviction spikes at ~1.3k evict/s. Throughput ~220 reqs/s per pod before spike. Observed p95 130ms, p99 720ms, p999 ~1.2s.
aj: Short excerpt from runtime logs during spike:
```
[2026-06-14T15:02:33Z] INFO serving: processed batch id=2456 size=12 latency=115ms kv_hits=0.82
[2026-06-14T15:02:33Z] WARN cache: eviction/sec=1320 evicted=1024 active_entries=49.1M
[2026-06-14T15:02:33Z] INFO kernel: selected=fused_attention_v2 fallback=gemm
[2026-06-14T15:02:33Z] ERROR service: request_id=xx p99_latency=720ms reason=kv_miss+evict_block
```
kai: Interesting — kernel switched to fused_attention_v2 but fallback to gemm indicated in same window. Could be contention on GPU memory allocator when eviction churn happens.
mary: Did you try lowering microbatch target or increasing cache size? Also curious if batching heuristics formed larger batches during ttl-induced misses.
aj: Quick A/B: same load with microbatch target 8 -> p99 drops to ~310ms, throughput down ~8%. With target 24 -> p99 spikes to ~980ms and throughput up 12% but tail worse.
sre-jen: That suggests an SLO tradeoff: smaller MB reduces latency tail at cost of throughput. But why eviction rate correlates — maybe MB size affects KV pressure because larger batches hold KV slots longer (longer KV pinning).
kai: Hypothesis: larger microbatches increase KV prefix reuse window, but when miss rate rises, the KV eviction worker runs harder and stalls allocator which blocks kernel memory pin/unpin. Need profile of allocator stalls and NVML GPU mem ops.
aj: I ran perf trace (simplified):
```
KV evict loop: avg_lock_wait=1.8ms -> spikes 12-18ms
GPU allocator lock: avg_wait=0.3ms -> during evict spike counter shows +15ms waits
RPC worker: queue_len spikes to 48
```
mary: Could also be kernel selection thrash: runtime switches kernels expecting certain workspace available, eviction concurrently frees memory and changes fragmentation -> fallback to slower kernel (gemm) for some batches causing tail.
kai: Good call. We should capture kernel choice per-batch correlated with eviction events. Add metric: kernel_used and fallback_reason per batch.
aj: Added to canary telemetry for next run. Also tried microbatch=8 + delayed eviction (increase soft_ttl by 200ms) on a replica: p99 ~250ms, throughput -10%. Eviction/sec peaked lower ~600/s.
sre-jen: Let's be careful with delayed eviction for production — can increase memory pressure. But useful for confirming causality.
dev-bot: deploy: canary updated aj/kv-tail-experiment -> rolled 2 pods with mb=8, eviction_soft_ttl=200ms at 2026-06-14T15:25:40Z
kai: Next steps:
- correlate per-batch kernel selection + alloc wait + kv_eviction_rate
- experiment microbatch target sweep [4,8,12,16,24] under 1k concurrent
- collect p95/p99/p999 and throughput, and eviction/sec and allocator wait hist
mary: Also run an experiment with kernel_force=fused_attention_v2 (no fallback) to see if avoiding fallback helps or exposes OOM/failure.
aj: One more datapoint: when we forced quantized kernel (lower workspace) tail stayed lower even with mb=24 (p99 ~360ms) but some samples showed increased hallucination-like token timing gaps — need QA. So quantized kernels help memory but can change output timing.
sre-jen: Good. Prioritize: 1) telemetry changes for kernel per-batch, 2) MB sweep against eviction rate, 3) allocator wait sampling, 4) conservative rollback plan.
aj: I'll share a short dashboard link once metrics are in: https://grafana.redwood/c/kv-tail/exp-171820
kai: Thanks — if anyone sees similar in other clusters ping here. :eyes:
mary: noted. thanks aj.
